short_answer: SportsCapPro is a small pick service covering college basketball, baseball, the NBA and football. Each play is rated 1 SOLID to 4 ELITE and, it says, comes with a written explanation. Its own site returned "480 Temporarily Unavailable" on 20 Nov 2026, so the only live place to buy is its CapperTek profile, where passes run from $15 for a day to $325 for 60 days and a 1 day free trial can be requested.

The record is the main finding. We downloaded the full CapperTek pick history and recounted it: 263 picks from 20 Feb 2025 to 25 Feb 2026, 118 wins, 143 losses and 2 pushes, 45% winners, -93.01 units on 1,950.1 units risked, an ROI of -4.77%. The service was hot from late Feb to mid Mar 2025 and then gave it back. The last 365 days were 16-29 and -85.53 units, and nothing has been logged in the 268 days since 25 Feb 2026.

Its own marketing told a different story. Archived pages advertised a "Consistent Winning Record," a rolling 67-44 run, and 58% and 59% seasons from before the CapperTek log began. Where we could put a claim next to the log, the log was weaker, and one blog run counted straight bets that CapperTek shows inside parlays.

Buyer reviews are few and all sit on CapperTek: four long positive reviews within 16 days of its first CapperTek pick in 2025, and one complaint about a $149 purchase with no picks that the same buyer withdrew the next day after the service "made it right." We found no Reddit, forum, BBB or news discussion of SportsCapPro at all.

guarantee: The archived All Sports page, saved on 18 May 2025, said the package "comes with a GUARANTEE that if you have not shown a PROFIT when the subscription expires you will receive an additional full year of our ALL SPORTS PACKAGE free of charge," and that the same applied to full season and combination packages. That is more picks, not money back, and it never covers what was lost on the bets.

The same founder's CapperTek bio mocks touts who promise "If This Bet Doesn't Win You Get the Rest of the Season (more LOSERS) Free". The extra year offer is a version of that model, so a buyer should weigh it the same way.

We saw no guarantee on the CapperTek pass page. CapperTek's terms, re-read on 20 Nov 2026, say "all fees and charges (including subscription fees) are non-refundable" unless otherwise stated. The archived SportsCapPro terms, dated 22 Jul 2021, contain no refund section at all; they disclaim warranties and say the laws of the United States govern.

claims_note: How we checked: on 20 Nov 2026 we downloaded SportsCapPro's complete CapperTek pick history (the all time filter) and recounted every graded pick by hand from the listed result and units. Our totals match CapperTek's own: 118-143-2, -93.01 units, ROI -4.77%. We then cut the same list by date windows to test each claim above.

The blog and the log are graded differently. On 6 Mar 2025 the blog wrote up Cal Poly -14 and UC Irvine -6.5 as two 4* ELITE straight bets. On CapperTek the same night shows a parlay of UC Irvine on the moneyline at -285 with Cal Poly -14, and a second parlay pairing UC Irvine with North Alabama. The 1 Mar 2025 blog recap lists eight straight bets at 5-3; CapperTek that day shows seven entries, three of them parlays, at 4-3. A buyer comparing the two cannot match them one to one.

The CapperTek reviewers describe seasons around 55% to 58% and a 39-21 March Madness in 2023, two years before the log begins, so we could not check them. Over the log they could check, the service won 45% of its picks.

Units do not line up. The bio and one reviewer describe a 1 to 4 unit scale, while the CapperTek log shows stakes from 4 to 11 units, most often 6 and 11. Judge the log by win rate and ROI rather than raw units: bet flat at 1 unit a pick, the 263 picks lost 12.6 units, about 4.8% of everything risked.
record: What is independently verifiable: CapperTek, not SportsCapPro, keeps the log. Every entry shows the game time, when the pick was made and when it was graded; we found no pick made after its listed start. Totals for 20 Feb 2025 to 25 Feb 2026: 263 picks, 118-143-2, 45% winners, -93.01 units on 1,950.1 units risked, ROI -4.77%. By sport: college basketball 166 picks (77-87-2, -12.50 units), baseball 73 (29-44, -94.15 units), NBA 19 (9-10), college football 3, NFL 1, NHL 1.

The timeline matters. From 20 Feb to 6 Mar 2025, the window when four positive reviews were posted, the log went 31-26 and +71.05 units. From 7 Mar to 8 Apr it went 37-44-2 and -23.53 units. May and June 2025, mostly baseball, cost 97.39 units across the two months. After a thin summer and autumn, Dec 2025 to Feb 2026 went 16-29 and -85.53 units, and the log then stops. Nothing has been posted in the 268 days to 20 Nov 2026.

Two details a buyer should know. First, 104 of the 263 picks (40%) were 2 pick parlays, often pairing a big moneyline favorite at -250 to -330 with a spread; they went 40-64. Second, 80 picks were posted as free picks, which went 34-45-1 and -65.11 units; the 183 paid picks went 84-98-1 and -27.90 units, ROI -1.88%. Paid picks were closer to break even, but still below it.

Limits of that log: CapperTek is paid by featured sellers, so it is not a neutral auditor. We could not see voided picks, and subscribers on SportsCapPro's own site may have received plays that were never posted on CapperTek. Football barely appears (4 picks), so the log says almost nothing about the NFL seasons the reviewers praise. Our web searches found no court or regulator action naming SportsCapPro.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition SportsCapPro is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about its picks beyond the CapperTek log described above.
our_data.context: For scale: SportsCapPro's reviewers describe seasons in the mid to high 50s by win rate, while its CapperTek log sits at 45%. On the Watchdog board on 20 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Every independent buyer review we found sits on CapperTek, a site SportsCapPro pays for featured placement and where it replies to reviews. We re-read all of them on 20 Nov 2026: six posts from five accounts, all from 2025, and nothing new since June 2025. We searched Reddit (through the Arctic Shift archive), Sportsbook Review, Covers, TheRX, BBB and the open web and found no other buyer talk about SportsCapPro.

customers.text: The buyer evidence is small and sits in one place. Four long, positive reviews landed on CapperTek between 28 Feb and 8 Mar 2025, within 16 days of the service's first CapperTek pick, and each describes years of profit with the service, a written reason with every play and a small number of plays. SportsCapPro replied warmly to each, in one case saying it remembered when the reviewer joined. Those weeks match the hottest stretch in its log. The only negative post came in June 2025, when a buyer said a $149 purchase (the price of its playoff special at the time) brought no picks and no reply; the next day the same buyer said the service had responded and made it right. No review from after the losing stretch exists, and we found no post about SportsCapPro on Reddit, forums, BBB or in the news. Treat the positives as testimony that cannot be checked against the log, which covers a later period and shows a loss.

A reviewer said following SportsCapPro brought significant profits and praised its clear, well researched analysis, especially in tournaments. No record or amount was given. SportsCapPro replied that the reviewer had joined a couple of years earlier.

A reviewer said he started with a one week package in Nov 2021 on a friend's tip, later moved to the yearly All Sports package, and has had no losing season overall in baseball, football or basketball since. He liked the small number of plays and the explanation with each one.
A reviewer who said he had lost with about six services over 20 years claimed a profit every season in each major sport over three years with SportsCapPro, betting its suggested unit sizes.

A reviewer said he joined in Feb 2023 on a friend's recommendation, that the March Madness package went 39-21, and that the service hits around 55% to 58% most seasons. Those figures are his and fall before the CapperTek log begins.
A buyer said he paid $149, never received a pick, and got no reply to calls, texts or emails, calling it "just another scam."
The next day the same buyer posted that SportsCapPro had finally responded and "made it right," and that he was withdrawing his complaint. He did not say what was done.
The site's homepage showed four testimonials signed with a first name and a town, praising steady bankroll growth, the analysis with each pick and NFL results. The seller chose and published them.

Our web searches for SportsCapPro, Sports Cap Pro and sportscappro.com found no Sportsbook Review, Covers or TheRX thread, no BBB profile and no news coverage. The Reddit archive queries that returned found no post naming it. SmartCustomer showed 0 reviews when we checked on 7 Nov 2026, and Trustpilot returned no page.

conflicts: SportsCapPro is a Pro Featured Verified service on CapperTek. CapperTek's FAQ, re-read on 20 Nov 2026, says Pro Featured services "pay us a nominal monthly advertising fee", and that "Verified" means the seller placed a CapperTek banner on its site so CapperTek has "an open line of communication" to resolve complaints. It is not an audit. The customer reviews are hosted on that same site, where SportsCapPro replies to them.
The seller grades its own blog runs and chose the testimonials on its homepage. The only record kept by someone else is the CapperTek log.
We saw no sportsbook affiliate links or promo codes on the archived SportsCapPro pages or on its CapperTek profile. We could not check its current site, which was offline.
strengths: A time stamped log kept by an outside site, with every pick made before the start, is more than many sellers offer, and it is complete enough to recount.
Many logged picks include a long written explanation, so a buyer can judge the reasoning rather than follow blind.
A $15 one day pass, or a free 1 day trial on request, allows a cheap test before a longer pass.
Paid picks were close to break even over 183 plays (ROI -1.88%), much better than the free picks.
A buyer's complaint about a missing purchase was resolved within a day, according to the buyer's own follow up.
concerns: The only full record shows a loss: 118-143-2 and -93.01 units over 263 picks, and 16-29 in the last 365 days.
No picks have been posted on CapperTek since 25 Feb 2026, and its own site was offline on 20 Nov 2026, so it is unclear what a buyer would receive today.
Advertised runs such as "67-44 (60%)" and "34-10" could not be matched to the log, and the blog grades straight bets that CapperTek records inside parlays.
About 40% of logged picks were 2 pick parlays, often built on heavy moneyline favorites, which is not what "sides and totals" buyers may expect.
Reviews are few, arrived in a 16 day cluster during a hot streak, and sit on a site the service pays.
The guarantee is an extra year of picks, not money back, and no owner or registered company is named.
checklist: Ask SportsCapPro whether its site will return and what you get today, given nothing has been logged on CapperTek since 25 Feb 2026.
Ask whether subscribers get the same plays as the CapperTek log, and whether 4* ELITE plays arrive as straight bets or parlays.
Open the CapperTek pick history with the "all time" filter, not the default 60 days, before you pay.
Count units and ROI, not wins. Check how much of the record is parlays.
Read any guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. This one is an extension.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It appears to be a real, small service: it sold passes on CapperTek from early 2025, logged 263 time stamped picks there, and one buyer said a missed delivery was put right. But its own site was offline on 20 Nov 2026, no picks have been logged since 25 Feb 2026, and no owner or registered company is named.

On CapperTek on 20 Nov 2026 a pass cost $15 for a day, $90 for 7 days, $140 for 14 days, $210 for 30 days or $325 for 60 days. Archived copies of its own site from May 2025 listed $10 day passes, sport packages from $49 a week or $399 a year, and All Sports at $699 a year.
Does SportsCapPro have a verified record?

The closest thing is its CapperTek log, which time stamps every pick. We recounted it on 20 Nov 2026: 118-143-2, -93.01 units, ROI -4.77% from Feb 2025 to Feb 2026. CapperTek is paid by featured sellers, and Watchdog has not graded SportsCapPro itself.
Do SportsCapPro's advertised runs hold up?

Not the ones we could test. A 28 day "67-44 (60%)" claim did not match any 28 day window on the log, and a "34-10" run used different counting from CapperTek, which shows many of those plays inside parlays. Its 58% and 59% seasons predate the log.
We found no cash refund. The archived All Sports package promised another year free if it ended without a profit, and CapperTek's terms say fees are non refundable unless stated otherwise.

You get a small number of rated plays with written analysis and a cheap one day pass to try it. What is unproven, and not supported by the only log we could open, is that the picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110; that log was at 45% winners and has been silent since February.
